articles.body: I trade crypto and write small bots in Python. Last week I wanted a side project that can earn something without clients and chats, so I tried Apify Store. In two days I published three Actors for Telegram. I used an AI coding assistant for most of the code, and I tested and published everything myself. This post is not a success story. I have zero paying users today. It is a list of what I built, what broke, and what I learned. The idea: no login, no API keys Every public Telegram channel has a web preview at t.me/s/channelname . It is plain HTML: posts, views, reactions, subscriber count. You don't need a Telegram account, a phone number or the official API. So all three Actors use only httpx and BeautifulSoup . No browser.

articles.title: Article 50(2) says the marking must be robust. I ran four checks and one failed.
articles.excerpt: Article 50(2) says the marking must be "robust". I ran four checks and one failed. Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act says synthetic audio, images, video and text have to be marked in a machine-readable f…
articles.body: Article 50(2) says the marking must be "robust". I ran four checks and one failed. Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act says synthetic audio, images, video and text have to be marked in a machine-readable format, detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Then it adds four properties the marking must satisfy: effective, interoperable, robust and reliable, as far as technically feasible. Four adjectives make a tidy sentence and a lousy test plan. I turned each one into a check I could actually run on my own image pipeline. One of them broke straight away. Effective: can anything read the mark at all? I embedded the IPTC trainedAlgorithmicMedia XMP block into a 64x64 PNG. The file went from 161 bytes to 974 bytes, and the verifier reported it marked.

articles.body: By Eric Gitangu. Originally published at developer.ericgitangu.com . I work on the backend of a mobility/fintech platform. This post is about three injection findings from an internal red-team pass, none of which involved a database, and about a fix I had to make twice. The problem Ask a team where they escape untrusted text and you get two answers: SQL and HTML. Those sinks have twenty years of bruises behind them. Two others in our backend did not. The log file. Our logger already masked contact data. It did not touch line breaks. Some log messages carry text that came from a request, and a line break in that text ends the real entry and starts a new line.

articles.body: Easy!Appointments OAuth calendar links carry booking and provider data across systems Easy!Appointments is an online scheduler. Customers choose a service and time, providers manage availability, and the system sends reminders and booking updates. Optional Google Calendar synchronization extends the workflow into an external identity and data boundary. A booking platform therefore holds customer details, provider schedules, and OAuth connections to another service. The official administrator guide says Easy!Appointments supports two-way sync with Google Calendar. Configuration requires a Google OAuth client, an authorized redirect URI, and credentials stored under Settings and then Integrations.

articles.title: Proxy or Redirect Private Downloads? What It Actually Costs
articles.excerpt: A discussion on r/node on November 20 raised a question worth examining: What happens to your bandwidth bill when you stream every private download through your application backend? It's a fair concer…
articles.body: A discussion on r/node on November 20 raised a question worth examining: What happens to your bandwidth bill when you stream every private download through your application backend? It's a fair concern. If every download passes through your application server, you're adding work to your infrastructure. But the actual cost depends heavily on where your files live, where your server runs, and what guarantees you need. Sometimes proxying costs more. Sometimes the difference is smaller than people expect. And sometimes choosing the cheaper option means giving up an important access guarantee. I've been working through this problem while building private file delivery infrastructure. Here is what I learned. Prices checked November 21, 2026. All prices are USD, at the time of writing. 1.

articles.title: Bee Releases Data Keys Only to Attested Instances and Publishes the Measurements
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Zero Operator Access is a design in which no operator, inside the company or inside the cloud provider, holds a technical path to customer data, and Bee, an Amazon company, built it for a wearab…
articles.body: TL;DR Zero Operator Access is a design in which no operator, inside the company or inside the cloud provider, holds a technical path to customer data, and Bee, an Amazon company, built it for a wearable personal AI device that records conversations. The AWS Architecture Blog published the architecture on 20 November 2026: a user's device releases the keys that decrypt their data only to EC2 instances whose boot measurements match an approved reference. The boot measurements carry the workload as well as the kernel: PCR4, PCR7 and PCR12 record the kernel image and Secure Boot state, and PCR14 is extended with one deterministic hash computed across the manifest, all container digests and all artifact checksums.

articles.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have caught a rare transitional phase at the end of a star's life, a fossilized remnant of stellar death throes, that could change our picture of the sun's final days.
articles.body: As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

articles.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
articles.excerpt: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is add…
articles.body: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers. As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening.

articles.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
articles.excerpt: A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another.
articles.body: (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system.
